Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan & next steps

Thanks again for the time this morning, Jordan — really helpful to surface the key success criteria. Per our call, I've attached a one-page MAP draft and a tech-eval checklist to kick off the technical milestone. High-level recap and proposed next steps: 

- Milestone: Technical evaluation (owned by Acme engineering + Redwood SE)
  - Target close: 2026-12-15 (aiming for decision for pilot by EoY)
  - Dependencies: access to sample PII-filtered dataset, SSO access to test environment, meeting with Acme infra on VPC egress
- Success criteria (benchmarks):
  - Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 250ms for 256-token prompts in our staging region
  - Cost target: average inference cost <= $0.003 / 1k tokens for production-like workload (we'll validate on your sample mix)
  - Quality: end-to-end pass-rate >= 90% on the 50-case eval prompt set you provided (NPS-style QA + hallucination threshold)
- Model shortlist (initial): Llama-3-8B-q4f, MosaicML-mpt-7b-instruct, Anthropic-claude-instant-1 (open to swapping based on repo access)
- Redwood deliverables:
  - Technical evaluation harness (benchmark scripts, perf traces) — due 12/6
  - Test deployment in dedicated sandbox (with KV/prefix caching enabled) — due 12/8

Can you confirm: 1) that Priya will own providing the sample dataset and SSO, 2) whether Acme infra can grant the temporary VPC peering/test egress by 12/6? If those are green, we'll schedule a kickoff with Marissa (our tech lead) for the evaluation plan review.

Attachment: acme_map_draft_v1.pdf (MAP draft)
Attachment: tech-eval-checklist.xlsx (checklist + template eval cases)

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

Thanks, Camila — great summary and appreciate the clear milestones. Quick answers inline: 

- Priya will own the dataset and SSO. Priya: I'll loop you to confirm when the scrubbed sample will be ready (aiming for 12/3).
- VPC peering / egress: infra is swamped this week, but we can get a temporary outbound rule by 12/7 if we prioritize. I'll push for 12/6 but can commit to 12/8 as fallback.

On the benchmarks: the latency target looks aggressive but acceptable as a starting point. Two asks from our side: 
1) Can Redwood provide 95th/99th latency at different sequence lengths (128/256/512) in the initial report?
2) For cost targets, can you clarify what's included in the $0.003/1k tokens (e.g., model-only inference or infra + egress)? We need an apples-to-apples number for our TCO model.

Also, model shortlist looks good. We are strongly inclined toward an 8B-class model for the pilot, but will confirm after Marissa's input.

I'll confirm dataset delivery timeframe by EOD tomorrow. Kickoff next week works for us.

Cheers,
Jordan Ellis

- Evaluation harness + sample scripts (Marissa) — by 2026-12-06

- Cost: $/1k tokens (model + instance compute) and expected per-request cost at 95th latency SLO
- Quality: top-line pass/fail vs your 50-case eval set + example failure modes (hallucinations, truncation, rate-limit behavior)

Open questions for Acme to confirm:
1) Can Priya provide the 50-case eval set in CSV + expected answers column? Preferred format: CSV with prompt, expected_answer, success_criteria
2) Any specific VPC IP ranges or proxy hostnames we should include in the test plan?

Notes on model shortlist: we'll prioritize 8B-class (Llama-3-8B-q4f) and include a slightly larger model (7–13B class) only if quality delta justifies cost delta. We'll also provide a quantized inference profile to show potential cost savings.
